confidential: Prepared for Epik High • Client proposal
heroBody: Use the new music to build demand for the shows. Use the shows to bring fans back to the music.
heroRecBody: Five focused city flights. Two lighter bursts. One connected release campaign.
artCaption: Official EPIKASE SONG BATTLE artwork • Released 04 Sep 2026
opportunityIntro: A three-song release gives the tour three fresh ways in. The job is to turn that attention into a reason to choose a show, then give the night a life beyond the venue.
opportunityBody: Recommend the $15K campaign because it carries the same three core markets into Chicago and Dallas, adds smaller Atlanta and Seattle bursts, and funds more creative tests. The $10K campaign stands on its own: keep the strongest three modeled listening markets and give each a properly weighted ticket flight.
insight1Title: Start where the music already travels.
insight1: Los Angeles, Toronto and New York lead the tour cities returned in Chartmetric’s modeled listening sample. Start there. Add Chicago next; give Dallas the additional full flight and Seattle only the added October 25 date. Seattle and Dallas estimates are too close to claim a meaningful demand difference.
insight2Title: Test the songs. Track the members.
insight2: The new tracks are credited to DJ TUKUTZ, TABLO and MITHRA JIN. Track each song directly, alongside Epik High’s group profile. Release-day streams and playlist data are unavailable in the API, so no song earns the lead by numbers yet.
insight3Title: A ticket link is not a sales report.
insight3: The tour has 14 listed shows in 13 markets. Public pages do not establish remaining inventory or an underselling city. Ticket allocations are conditional on promoter confirmation; the October 22 Seattle show is reported sold out and receives no ticket-acquisition budget.
baselineNote: Chartmetric API, retrieved Sep 4, 2026. Aug 31 non-interpolated endpoints; monthly listeners are rolling 28-day unique listeners, not streams. Followers are cumulative profile follows, not an addressable advertising list. These are pre-campaign observations, not campaign results.
releaseTitle:
Three personalities.
One Epik High night.
releaseIntro: Working release: EPIKASE SONG BATTLE, September 4, 2026. Apple Music, the official artist smartlink and Chartmetric agree on the release and track identities.
releaseAssumption: The quoted request is undated. We interpret “came out today” as the verified September 4 release, not as a confirmed timestamp for the original message. Confirm this release scope at kickoff.
track1Body: The official episode gives TUKUTZ a dance-led, larger-than-life reveal. Start with that visual energy for the ticket invitation; test it against TABLO’s more intimate treatment.
track2Body: TABLO describes the song as quiet comfort for his wife. Test a companionship-led invitation with the performance section and BANG YEDAM’s feature credit.
track3Body: MITHRA JIN’s NELL-produced song brings a singing-led contrast. Test that unexpected side for listening and for reflective, cleared morning-after recaps.
videoNote: The official EPIKASE episode contains performance chapters at 10:51, 28:02 and 41:33. These are source chapters, not final ad edit points. Edit selections require the original files, music/likeness clearance and team approval. Tour setlist inclusion is not assumed.
channelTitle: One paid platform. Two clear destinations.
channelBody: Use Meta placements across Instagram and Facebook: Reels, Stories and Feed. Begin with eligible artist-engagement/video-viewer audiences where available and a consolidated local prospecting audience. Never imply that Spotify listener estimates can be uploaded as targetable fans. Test broad local reach against music-interest signals only where the account supports them.
channelBody2: Keep at most two creative variants active per city. Start with TUKUTZISM and anime; promote a challenger only when it earns stronger ticket-page or listening-link response. No separate TikTok, YouTube, search, creator-buy or playlist-purchase budget at these investment levels.
destination1Body: City-specific ad → official city ticket page. One primary action: get tickets. Use purchase optimization only when validated ticketing events and enough signal are available; otherwise measure ticket-page visits.
destination2Body: Song or recap ad → approved release smartlink. One primary action: listen. Use the existing official link initially; use the team’s measurable smartlink if analytics access is supplied. An outbound service click is not a completed stream.
waveTitle: Make every supported night a wave.
waveIntro: Anticipation. The live moment. The return to the music. CCD’s “dopamine wave” is a campaign-planning rhythm, not a scientific claim or a promise of algorithmic lift.
waveCaption: Conceptual emphasis across a show cycle. Not audience, sales or performance data.
waveBeforeBody: Localized new-song edits earn attention; city, venue and date make the invitation concrete. Full flights run 14 days before each show. Lighter flights use the final five days. Stop at the ticket cutoff, or earlier if sold out.
waveLiveBody: Artist Stories, approved venue screens and available live footage connect the evening to the release. Organic capture is the default. No paid show-day ticket line, on-site crew or guaranteed artist post is assumed.
waveAfterBody: Publish a timely recap with an explicit listening link. Full-support cities receive $200 across four days. Only use cleared footage and eligible engagement audiences; if too small, consolidate local delivery. Light cities receive an organic recap opportunity.
waveRule: One edit, one ask. A recap can become a ticket ad for the next included city only after replacing the location and CTA. If footage is late, use an approved release edit; do not spend simply to fill a calendar.
marketsTitle:
Concentrate the spend.
Keep the whole tour in view.
marketsIntro: Audience geography is the starting signal. Remaining tickets, time to show, approved assets and achievable daily spend determine the final allocation. No market is labeled as underselling.
geoSubtitle: Estimated Spotify monthly listeners by city • Sep 4, 2026
geoNote: Chartmetric modeled estimates, not ticket demand, unique targetable fans or observed city growth. The six other tour markets were absent from the returned 46-city sample; absence does not mean no audience. City boundaries can overlap, so totals are not added. Ticketing needs can override this starting order.
scheduleNote: All 14 shows are upcoming as of Sep 4, 2026. Ticket pages are linked from the official artist hub. Listings confirm an event, not inventory. Recheck each sale before the flight starts.
soldoutNote: October 22 Seattle was reported sold out in the August 9 tour press release. Retain organic release/fan-content opportunities; no acquisition spend. October 25 is the separate added show. Reconfirm with the promoter.
priorityRule: If a selected city has no acquisition need, first deepen another included city with verified need. Adding a replacement market requires an agreed scope swap. Keep the total fixed; hold unneeded funds rather than forcing delivery.
creativeTitle:
The ads should sound
like Epik High.
creativeIntro: Member chemistry, contrasting tracks and the EPIKASE battle give us the creative premise. These are proposed treatments, not claims about proven conversion. Approved English captions keep the ideas understandable without erasing the original voices.
concept1Title: Your favorite group chat. In person.
concept1Hook: Use TUKUTZ’s dance-led performance reveal and the members’ comic chemistry, then cut into TUKUTZISM. Finish with the show’s city and date. The feeling is a reunion with the group, not a generic tour poster.
concept1Meta: 10–15 seconds • 9:16 + 4:5 • local fans and new music audiences • pre-show
concept1Copy: “Your favorite group chat. In person. Epik High · Toronto · October 4.”
concept1Asset: Official TUKUTZISM performance chapter starts at 41:33. Adaptable after source-file and music/likeness clearance; no new shoot.
concept2Hook: TABLO frames anime around companionship and silent comfort. A subtitled introduction into the performance gives a friend-to-friend invitation a reason to exist.
concept2Meta: 15 seconds • 9:16 + 4:5 • artist engagers and local prospects • pre-show
concept2Copy: “Bring someone who gets it. Epik High · New York · September 30.”
concept2Asset: Official anime chapter starts at 10:51. Approve the excerpt and English subtitle meaning. No promise that the track or its guest will appear in the tour set.
concept3Title: You know the voice. Hear another side.
concept3Hook: Let MITHRA JIN’s singing-led performance interrupt expectations. Use one song and one member per listening version, then make the destination explicit.
concept3Meta: 10–15 seconds • 9:16 + 4:5 • included package markets only • ongoing release
concept3Copy: “MITHRA JIN · Will I Be Okay. Hear another side.”
concept3Cta: Listen to Will I Be Okay
concept3Asset: Official MITHRA JIN chapter starts at 28:02. Cleared artwork/audio are the immediate fallback. The official song battle ends September 14; do not extend voting into the tour.
concept4Hook: Open with a cleared moment from that exact city, then use anime or Will I Be Okay as the recap soundtrack. Reconnect the memory with an intentional listen.
concept4Meta: 10–20 seconds • 9:16 + 4:5 • eligible engagers in the played city • post-show
concept4Copy: “Last night stays with you. Take the night home.”
concept4Cta: Listen to Will I Be Okay
concept4Asset: Requires timely artist/venue footage or separately cleared fan content. New filming and fan-rights acquisition are excluded; approved release artwork is the fallback.
creativeFoot: Sample copy is for approval. No quoted lyrics, fabricated endorsements or unverified performance claims. A template can be prepared now; a live recap is produced only from supplied, cleared material.
swshTitle:
Let the night
live in one place.
swshTag: Optional partner activation • outside both packages
swshIntro: A shared swsh album can turn scattered fan angles into a collective show memory, with a clear route back to EPIKASE. Start with a separately scoped two-show pilot only if the team can distribute and moderate it.
swshVerified: Verified: shared photo/video albums, link/QR entry, browser participation and custom outbound links. Commercial plans list analytics and custom upload agreements. Branded artist services require the appropriate commercial scope.
swshScope: Potential distribution: artist Stories, a merch-table QR or venue-approved screens, and a promoter message to its eligible audience. CCD supplies the creative/links; the tour team secures placement and approved assets; a named moderator reviews uploads. Artist participation and venue distribution must be confirmed. The vendor configures the albums and agreed reporting exports. A separately consented follow-up can send the recap and listening link; confirm channel permissions and the sending platform before use.
swshRights: Three separate permissions: participating in the album; allowing specific content and recognizable likenesses to be reused, especially in ads; and choosing email/SMS marketing. Uploaders retain ownership under swsh terms. Download access is not an advertising license, and album membership is not marketing consent.
swshCost: Public plans list Starter at $100/month and Growth at $250/month; Enterprise is quoted. These are software entry prices, not an Epik High activation quote. Custom branding, moderation, rights work, participant capacity and CCD execution must be scoped separately. No vendor cost is hidden in either package.
swshNoPromise: An outbound music link is feasible. Native streaming attribution, automatic retargeting access and guaranteed engagement are not assumed. Confirm analytics/export definitions and applicable age, privacy and consent requirements before activating.
investmentIntro: Total campaign investment in USD, with fees inside the ceiling. These are scoped planning allocations, not an approved CCD rate card. Final fees, payment terms and scope are confirmed in the campaign agreement. swsh and other vendors are additional only if separately agreed.
expandedDesc: More of the tour, with enough weight to matter.
focusedGeo: Full: New York, Toronto, Los Angeles.
expandedGeo: Full: New York, Toronto, Los Angeles, Chicago, Dallas. Light: Atlanta, Seattle (Oct 25).
focusedDeliverables: 6 master edits: 4 ticket treatments (2 songs × 2 hooks), 1 listening edit and 1 recap template. Up to 6 localized ticket versions and 3 finished city recaps. Two aspect ratios per delivered version; one consolidated revision round.
expandedDeliverables: 9 master edits: 6 ticket treatments (2 songs × 3 hooks), 2 listening edits and 1 recap template. Up to 12 localized ticket versions (2 per full city, 1 per light city) and 5 finished city recaps. Two aspect ratios per delivered version; one consolidated revision round.
masterNote: City versions adapt approved masters, not additional creative concepts. Both scopes include one campaign setup, link/tracking QA, twice-weekly optimization, weekly reporting and a final readout. Recaps delivered within one business day of receiving cleared footage, subject to agreed turnaround and approvals.
deltaMediaBody: Two added full city flights, two light bursts, $800 more ongoing release support and two more paid city recaps.
deltaCreativeBody: Three extra master treatments, six more localized ticket versions and two more finished recaps.
deltaMgmtBody: Ten additional campaign days and the extra city reporting/optimization scope.
mediaNote: Core flights average $114/day over 14 days; added full cities $79/day; light bursts $60/day over five days. Recaps average $50/day for four days. These are budget allocations, not performance forecasts.
poolNote: The $40/day or $48/day release pool starts in the core three markets. The $10K pool stays within New York, Toronto and Los Angeles; the $15K pool may rotate among its seven included markets as shows approach or pass. It is one consolidated pool, not equal daily spend in every city. The expanded flight continues through Oct 29; only the five full-support cities get dedicated paid recaps. Keep audiences consolidated and cap simultaneous creative tests.
exclusions: Excluded: ad spend beyond the ceiling, new shoots/on-site crews, paid creators, PR, guaranteed playlists, ticketing/platform fees, new landing-page development, CRM build, swsh, vendor moderation and fan-content rights procurement. Artist/team supplies approved media, captions, ad access, destination links and timely content. No ad launch or spend commitment is created by this proposal.
calendarAssumption: Planning start: September 10, assuming approvals and access by September 8. If onboarding slips, shorten or swap flights within scope; never backdate spend or add budget to preserve an obsolete calendar.
measureTitle:
Measure the action.
Respect the limits.
measureIntro: We commit to the scoped work and transparent decisions. Ticket sales, streams, followers and reach are observed outcomes. No modeled sales or streaming forecast is presented because no campaign-specific benchmark has been verified.
measureTicket: Report spend, impressions, reach, frequency, ticket-link visits and cost per visit by city. Call clicks “clicks” if destination landing-page measurement is unavailable. Report attributable purchases/return only after ticketing events are validated; otherwise use promoter-supplied city sales trends as context, not causal proof.
measureMusic: Report smartlink visits and outbound streaming-service clicks when access permits. Track all three release IDs, Epik High’s group profile and relevant member profiles. Compare first complete seven-day track windows, then like-for-like weekly windows; do not compare a partial release day with a full week. Artist trends use fixed-date, rolling 28-day listener snapshots and cumulative followers.
measureSwsh: Subject to the contracted dashboard/export: joins, unique uploaders, approved assets, assets cleared for organic/paid reuse, separate marketing opt-ins, and tagged listening-link activity. Define each denominator before reporting participation rates. An upload or opt-in does not prove a stream or sale.
optTitle: A weekly decision, not just a report.
opt1: Daily: check delivery, broken links, spend pacing and ticket status. Pause a sold-out show immediately. Before launch, test destinations and any purchase events with the ticketing partner.
opt2: Twice weekly: compare creative within the same city, objective and window. Use three days and roughly 75 measured destination visits as a provisional review gate, not a statistical guarantee. Keep no more than two variants active; inspect placement quality and frequency before favoring a cheaper click.
opt3: Scale or move: shift the next tranche toward verified ticket need and stronger qualified response. A 30% cost difference is a review trigger, not proof of a winner. If purchases are sparse, report the limitation. If content, tracking or demand is inadequate, consolidate, hold or stop; do not spend to meet a chart.
opt4: Weekly: reconcile media with city ticket reports, refresh song/artist snapshots and document changes. Final readout within five business days after the package ends. No ticket- or stream-sale guarantees.
